assumptions: Daniel is Player One and Nik is Player Two; both enter their real signings fairly.
Chromium runs the unchanged local game screens. A prepared, already-started Showdown uses the real transfer rules in Node and retains locked moves between page loads.
title: Typing a shared league name locks Argentina without choosing a country
steps: Start season 1 of a 3-season Showdown and finish the transfer window.
Nik chooses the Spain Primera División league guess; both friends lock their guesses.
Daniel enters a signing name, types Primera División as the previous league, and chooses Brazil as the nationality. Do not choose a league country from the list.
Daniel locks his signing; Nik locks his signings; read the reveal.
expected: The game asks Daniel to choose Spain or Argentina before locking this shared league name. A signing from Spain must be released when Nik guessed Spain.
actual: The field silently chooses argentina-primera-division while displaying only Primera División. The signing locks and the Spain guess gives a KEEP verdict.
root_cause: The league-name lookup keeps the first league for a shared name. Typing an exact label immediately fills that league choice, and signing validation accepts it. The list does show both countries and an explicit Spain selection works; it is the unchosen typed label that is accepted incorrectly.

fix.change: Only accept an exact typed label automatically when it names one league. For shared labels, require an explicit country choice before locking; preserve saved league IDs and explicit list choices.
